defects.summary: hooks/event-ledger/ledger.py performs NO redaction. Any text passed to note.py (the tool AGENTS.md section 3 mandates for recording decisions and failures) is written verbatim to stdout and persisted verbatim to ~/.claude/event-ledger/<project>/events.jsonl, including OpenAI-shaped sk- keys that every other component in this repo masks. Repo and deployed copy are byte-identical (sha256 9db70a3552223a66), so the exposure is live, and the ledger is durable append-only storage that survives compaction. FIX: route fields through the existing agent-self/harness/redaction.py::redact_text before the append, and route note.py's echo through it too.

tools/mcp/qdx-rush-mcp/qdx_mcp_server.py::qdx_whoami emits rush_token_tail = RUSH_TOKEN[-6:] into an MCP tool result while its docstring asserts it 'does not expose the token'. A suffix is the high-entropy end of a credential; the sanctioned disclosure is a zero-entropy PREFIX. FIX: replace the tail with a length + a zero-entropy prefix, or drop the field; and correct the docstring.

Three divergent redactors with no shared floor: agent-self/harness/redaction.py, ci/harness/redaction.py and skills/workflow-monitor/monitorcore/redact.py each miss credential shapes the others catch (standalone JWT; ghr_/htk_; and any generic key=value or Bearer rule respectively). A credential redacted on one surface is emitted on another. Notably, the estate's real credential stores (~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json) hold JWTs, and the redactor guarding the event ledger is the one with no JWT pattern. FIX: promote ONE pattern set to a shared module and have all three import it.

The generic credential pattern in both harness redactors requires a literal ':' or '=' separator, so a SPACE-separated CLI flag ('--api-key <value>', '--token <value>') defeats it even though the credential-naming flag is adjacent. Measured live against EventLedger.append (T11-cli-flag-space leaked). FIX: add a separator class that includes whitespace after a credential-named flag.

htk_query.py::_key() silently falls back to HKCU\Environment, so an operator who scrubs the process environment still ships the credential on the wire and cannot force the credential-absent branch. This is a correctness hazard for any incident response that assumes 'unset the variable' disables a key, and it defeated two of this unit's own probes. FIX: make the registry fallback opt-in (or log 'source=registry' at zero entropy) so the credential's provenance is visible.

report.question: Does every credential-touching code path (presence checks, auth probes, error messages, logs, ledger entries, crash dumps) emit at most a zero-entropy prefix - and does any path print, persist or transmit the value?
report.answer: NO - not every path. Of 13 enumerated targets, 3 are CONFIRMED to emit more than a zero-entropy prefix, 4 are PARTIAL (they redact some shapes and pass others through), and 6 are REFUTED (no value emission under the branches exercised). The single worst finding is T10: hooks/event-ledger/ledger.py applies NO redaction whatsoever, so a credential mentioned in a note.py entry - the very tool AGENTS.md section 3 mandates for recording failures - is printed to stdout and persisted verbatim to durable append-only storage, in every shape tested including the sk- vendor shape that every other component masks. The second is T12: qdx_whoami discloses a 6-character token SUFFIX (the high-entropy end) while its docstring claims it does not expose the token. The third is T7b: htk_query.py's registry fallback means a credential is still read and transmitted after the environment variable has been removed. The paths that behaved correctly did so by NAMING rather than SHOWING - the per-edit secret gate reports 'OpenAI API key on line 1', the deny guard returns a fixed constant, the account store reports only the parser's position - which is exactly the zero-entropy contract the question asks for.
report.verdict_semantics: Each target row carries exactly one verdict answering: DOES THIS PATH PRINT, PERSIST OR TRANSMIT THE PLANTED VALUE? CONFIRMED = yes, executable-proven. REFUTED = no, across every branch exercised. PARTIAL = leaks in some exercised shapes and not others. NOT-CHECKED = no probe ran. BLOCKED = a probe was attempted and could not reach the branch.

detector_failures.symptom: All four T8 runs reported leaked=False with exit 0.
detector_failures.root_cause: The driver called accounts.AccountStore(path) but the constructor is AccountStore(path, policies), so every run died with a TypeError BEFORE reaching _load(). The credential-store error branch was never executed; the four 'no leak' readings measured nothing.
detector_failures.repair: PROBE 2b passes policies=[] and asserts the branch was reached by printing 'LOADED-OK keys=[...]' on the happy path and by showing the AccountStoreLoadError text on each failure path.

detector_failures.found_in: PROBE 2 run T7-key-unset, then PROBE 2b run T7-key-truly-unset
detector_failures.symptom: Two consecutive runs intended to exercise the credential-absent branch instead authenticated successfully.
detector_failures.root_cause: Strike 1: htk_query._key() falls back to HKCU\Environment, so scrubbing the child env does not remove the credential. Strike 2: shadowing winreg via PYTHONPATH cannot work because winreg is a BUILT-IN module (sys.builtin_module_names -> True, winreg.__file__ absent).
detector_failures.repair: Two strikes on one hypothesis triggered a pivot (AGENTS.md 4b): three alternatives were enumerated before attempt 3, and the chosen one - poisoning sys.modules['winreg'] from a sitecustomize.py that runs before the main script - reached the branch on the first try ('error: HACKTRICKS_API_KEY is not set'). The root cause itself became finding T7b.

detector_failures.symptom: A SELF-CONTRADICTING result: the run's own stdout showed 'text': 'repro: [REDACTED] then rerun' while the file sweep simultaneously reported the canary inside events.jsonl.
detector_failures.root_cause: All T10/T11 cases shared one sandbox and one ledger root. The sweep flagged any file that had been modified and then searched the WHOLE file, so bytes appended by EARLIER cases were attributed to the current one. A self-contradicting output is a detector failure, not a finding.
detector_failures.repair: PROBE 2d gives every case its own fresh sandbox and ledger root AND compares only the bytes appended since the run started. Its both-states control (NC4/NC5) was re-proven after the repair, because the pre-repair control did not cover this failure mode. The corrected result changed two verdicts: T11-env-assign and T11-vendor-shape are NOT leaks.

extensions.hard_constraint_disclosure: The catalog's HARD CONSTRAINT is 'no real credential is read, printed, rotated, revoked, unset or modified'. One clause was touched and is disclosed here rather than buried. During PROBE 2 run T7-key-unset and PROBE 2b run T7-key-truly-unset, the code under test (htk_query.py) resolved the REAL HACKTRICKS_API_KEY from HKCU\Environment and sent it as an X-API-Key header to a LOCAL 127.0.0.1 test server started by this probe. That is a READ, and it was not intended - it is the very behaviour that became finding T7b. Mitigations and verification: (a) the destination was loopback only, never a network egress; (b) the value was never printed - the only rendering of it anywhere was the code-under-test's own '***REDACTED***'; (c) a vendor-prefix regex scan (htk_|sk-|gh[pousr]_|hf_|xox[baprs]-) over all 14 sandbox files and over probe2.json/probe2.err returned exactly one hit, and it was this unit's own synthetic sk- canary; (d) all 15 sandboxes were deleted and verified gone; (e) nothing was rotated, revoked, unset or modified - AGENTS.md section 9 forbids an agent doing any of those, and none was attempted. The subsequent presence diagnosis (present, 68 chars, prefix htk_) is the read-only form section 9 explicitly permits. RECOMMENDATION TO THE OWNER, not an action taken: no rotation is indicated by this event on its own, because the value never left loopback and never reached durable storage - but if ADV-0023's corpus sweep finds credential material in ~/.claude/event-ledger (see residual_unknowns[1], the D1 blast radius), that IS a rotation trigger and the decision belongs to the owner.
extensions.blast_radius_D1: hooks/event-ledger/ledger.py is byte-identical in the repo and at ~/.claude/hooks/event-ledger/ledger.py (sha256 9db70a3552223a66), so the defect is live, not theoretical. Its reachable consumers are note.py (invoked by name in .agents/skills/grill-with-docs, prototype/SKILL.md, prototype/LOGIC.md, prototype/UI.md and to-prd/SKILL.md, and mandated by AGENTS.md section 3), append_claim_edge, and stop-hook.py. stop-hook.py is NOT an exposure - it appends only git head/branch/dirty-count and a 12-char session id. The exposure surface is therefore agent- and operator-authored note TEXT, which is exactly where a pasted repro command carrying a token would land, and the sink is durable append-only storage that survives compaction and is replayed at SessionStart.

extensions.sha256_convention: artifacts[0].bytes is the exact size of this file on disk. artifacts[0].sha256 is the SHA-256 of this file's bytes with the artifacts[0].sha256 field replaced by 64 '0' characters -- the only self-consistent way to record a receipt's own digest inside itself.
